headlines.title: Analog Devices (ADI) Stock Fair Value Moves Lower After Mixed Analyst Target Revisions
headlines.summary: Analog Devices is back in focus after the Fair Value Estimate in one model was reduced from US$470.72 to US$441.34, a modest cut of around 6%. This move sits alongside recent research where some firms raised targets into the mid US$500s while others trimmed forecasts by US$50 to US$100. This reflects a split view on near term execution and spending. As you read on, you will see how these shifting targets feed into the broader analyst narrative and what to watch as the story evolves.

headlines.title: Analog Devices keeps UBS target despite softer earnings guidance
headlines.summary: Analog Devices Inc (NASDAQ:ADI) retained its “buy” rating and $420 price target at UBS despite weaker-than-expected earnings guidance and plans to more than double capital spending in fiscal 2027. headlines.title: Analog Devices Just Plunged After Earnings. Is Its Dividend Now a Bargain?
headlines.summary: Record revenue, a clear earnings beat, and still a 17% one-day wipeout. Analog Devices has raised its payout for 22 straight years, but one number in its outlook could decide whether that streak survives the AI boom.

headlines.title: Chip Stocks Just Pulled a Whipsaw Last Seen at the April 2025 Tariff Pause
headlines.summary: A CEO reinstatement sent chip stocks soaring one day and a fresh selloff erased most of it the next. Only two other sessions in three decades looked like this, and one involved a pandemic. What does the speed of the giveback reveal?

headlines.title: Analog Devices: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
headlines.summary: The company is spending $1.6 billion to $1.9 billion on new capacity in fiscal 2027, a bet that will shape how much growth turns into shareholder cash.

description: Analog Devices, Inc. engages in the design, manufacture, testing, and marketing of integrated circuits (ICs), software, and subsystems products in the United States, rest of North and South America, Europe, Japan, China, and rest of Asia. It provides data converter products, which translate real-world analog signals into digital data, as well as translates digital data into analog signals; power management and reference products for power conversion, driver monitoring, sequencing, and energy management applications in the automotive, communications, industrial, and consumer markets; and power ICs that include performance, integration, and software design simulation tools for accurate power supply designs. The company also offers amplifiers to condition analog signals; and radio frequency and microwave ICs to support cellular infrastructure; and micro-electro-mechanical systems technology solutions, including accelerometers used to sense acceleration, gyroscopes for sense rotation, inertial measurement units to sense multiple degrees of freedom, and broadband switches for radio and instrument systems, as well as isolators. In addition, it provides digital signal processing and system products for numeric calculations. The company serves clients in the industrial, automotive, consumer, instrumentation, aerospace, defense and healthcare, and communications markets through a direct sales force, third-party distributors, and independent sales representatives, as well as online. The company was incorporated in 1965 and is headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts.
